ltv_slabs._note: RBI standard three-slab. Boundaries <=30L, 30-75L, >75L, on property value. NOTE: Bajaj is an HFC - some HFCs stretch LTV higher than banks; this page only states generic RBI ceiling, not Bajaj-specific policy. Confirm Bajaj's actual max on product page/DSA.
ltv_slabs._source: Bajaj Housing resource page on LTV (bajajhousingfinance.in) - describes RBI standard, not Bajaj-specific.

retirement_age._note: Salaried 67, self-employed/professional 70 at maturity. More generous than most banks on salaried (beats HDFC 60, ICICI 65, Axis 65; below SBI 70). HFC flexibility. Co-applicant can extend for older applicants.

min_cibil._source: Bajaj insights/blog article (bajajfinserv.in) - NOT the eligibility criteria page
min_cibil._note: Blog states 725 min, 750+ ideal for best rates (7.25%). 725-749 = additional evaluation, not auto-approve. TENSION: this looks stricter than banks, yet Bajaj's rate goes to 20% (only makes sense if it lends to weak profiles). Likely 725 is standard-product soft floor; sub-725 underwritten case-by-case at high rates, OR via other products. Blog-tier, soft figure. DSA-gated: confirm Bajaj's real hard floor and how the 20% borrowers qualify.

processing_fee._note: HFC wide range: 0.25%-2% typical, up to 4% for weak profiles + 18% GST. FAR higher ceiling than banks (HDFC/ICICI 0.5%, Axis 1%). Negotiable down toward 0.25% for 750+ CIBIL / strong profile / existing customer / promo. Same HFC pattern as rate: cheap for prime, expensive for risky. Other charges deferred.
processing_fee._source: Bajaj Housing Finance home loan fees page (bajajhousingfinance.in)

rate_band._note: HFC structure: prime floor competitive (salaried 7.25% ties SBI as lowest), but ceiling 20% - FAR above any bank (HDFC 13.2, ICICI 9.8, Axis 9.1, SBI 8.55). This IS the HFC model: lends to weak/thin profiles banks decline, at punishing rates. Self-employed floor 7.70% (premium vs salaried). Repo-linked.
rate_band._source: Bajaj Housing Finance home loan rate page (bajajhousingfinance.in)

foir_by_income_band._note: FOIR cap varies by income - proprietary, DSA-gated

salaried: 6 months bank statement (salary credits + EMI deductions)
Employment stability proof - salary certificate/appointment/increment letter, min 3 yrs work stability
self_employed_professional: Audited P&L + Balance Sheet 2-3 years (CA certified)
Business continuity proof (GST/Trade License/Incorporation) - min 3-5 yrs vintage
self_employed_non_professional: Audited P&L + Balance Sheet 2-3 years (CA certified)
Business existence proof (GST/Trade License/Partnership Deed/ROC) - min 3-5 yrs vintage
accepted_income_proofs._note: From official Bajaj docs pages. HFC asks a RANGE (2-3 yrs ITR/financials) - more flexible than fixed bank requirements. Requires MIN 3 YRS work stability (salaried) and 3-5 YRS business vintage (self-employed) - stricter on stability/vintage than some banks. NRI docs exist, not modeled.
accepted_income_proofs._source: Bajaj Finserv + Bajaj Housing Finance docs pages (bajajfinserv.in, bajajhousingfinance.in)

co_applicant_clubbing._note: Key remediation lever for FOIR-bound buyers. Clubbing spouse/parent income raises FOIR base. Haircut % and allowed relationships are lender-specific - DSA-gated. Co-applicant's own EMIs usually also clubbed.
